## How to read this document

Companion to `Hero_Numbers.Rmd`, which covers the Main Text tab. Same rules:

- **Bold is the CURRENT value** — the number to write with.
- ~~Struck and greyed~~ is the superseded published value, kept only so you can
  find the sentence it replaces.
- Anything that appears in a figure is read **from that figure's own saved data
  object**, so the text and the figure cannot disagree.

Each claim gets an id, the sentence as it reads in the Doc today, the code that
regenerates it, and the current value.

---

# Part 0 — Structural problems that are not about numbers

These need fixing regardless of which values you use. None of them are
recomputable; they are inconsistencies within the document as written.

```{r structural, echo=FALSE}
struct <- data.frame(
  id = c("X1","X2","X3","X4","X5","X6","X7"),
  problem = c(
    "Front matter says **Figs. S1 to S9**",
    "Front matter says **Tables S1 to S8**",
    "Two different sections are both numbered **S5**",
    "Section S7 cites fig. **S13A/B/C** for correlation, Meff and cumulative score",
    "Section S7 cites fig. **S7D** for the by-cohort cumulative-score contribution",
    "Section S3 cites fig. **S4A-C** for the ZIP country result",
    "Sections S5/S7 cite **Fig. 3A** and **Fig. 3B** of the main text"),
  reality = c(
    "There are now 22 supplementary figures (S1-S22). Added this cycle: matrix confound (S20, 2026-08-11), year trends (S12), population structure (S21), estimator comparison (S22), analyte overlap (S3) and the three determinants figures (S8-S10, 2026-11-17)",
    "Methods cites Table S9 twice (location-only model; within-cohort models)",
    "'S5 Demographics Associated with Exposure Levels' and 'S5 Quantile Power Analysis'",
    "Those panels are Figure **S14**A/B/C. S13 is the QQ-plot figure",
    "That panel is Figure **S14D**",
    "ZIP is Figure **S5**. S4 is TEDDY",
    "Figure 3 was replaced this cycle with the ExWAS/pooling figure. Its panels are now spread(z), decomposition, divergence and variance-share -- neither the dispersion metric nor the sociodemographic model bars are in it any more"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(struct, col.names = c("id","reads","should read"))
```

> **X7 is the one that matters most.** Two supplementary sections point the
> reader at main-text Figure 3 panels that no longer contain what the sentence
> describes. The dispersion values (MDUC, DAPS, MEBCO, TSIC) and the
> sociodemographic model bars now live in the within-study supplementary figure,
> not Figure 3.

---

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)

ROOT <- Sys.getenv("HHEAR_ROOT", normalizePath(".."))   # knit from Coding/
OUT  <- file.path(ROOT, "Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2")
HARM <- file.path(ROOT, "Input/Harmonized_Datasets")
HN   <- file.path(ROOT, "Output/Hero_Numbers")
dir.create(HN, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

LEDGER <- list()
hero <- function(id, section, claim, published, now, note = "") {
  LEDGER[[length(LEDGER) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
    id = id, section = section, claim = claim,
    published = as.character(published), now = as.character(now),
    note = note, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  invisible(NULL)
}

load1 <- function(path) { e <- new.env(); load(path, envir = e); get(ls(e)[1], envir = e) }
# Read a ggplot's own data, so a number can never drift from its figure.
figdata <- function(path) as.data.table(load1(path)$data)
pct <- function(x, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), x)
```

```{r load-data}
H <- as.data.table(load1(file.path(HARM, "Harmonized_Targeted.RData")))
H[, Std := sub("_Targeted$", "", Study)]
H[, pid := fcoalesce(as.character(Child_PID), as.character(Mat_PID))]
H[, Pop := fifelse(!is.na(Child_PID), "Child", "Adult")]

# RULE (same as the main ledger): dilution markers are not exposures.
EXP <- H[!Analyte_Code %in% c("CRE", "SG")]

S <- as.data.table(load1(file.path(HARM, "Harmonized_SDOH.RData")))
S[, Std := sub("_SDOH$", "", Study)]

# Most common category of a demographic field within one study, as a percent of
# the non-missing responses in that study. This is the rule the S1 sentences use.
topcat <- function(col, std, k = 1) {
  x <- S[Std == std & !is.na(get(col)) & !get(col) %in% c("", "NA"), as.character(get(col))]
  if (!length(x)) return(NA_character_)
  t <- sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE)
  if (k > length(t)) return(NA_character_)
  sprintf("%s %s", names(t)[k], pct(100 * as.numeric(t[k]) / length(x), 0))
}
```

# Part 1 — Methods

## M1. Which biospecimen matrix

> **CLAIM (Methods, para 3).** "The chemical exposures measured in blood were
> trace elements in <span style='color:#999'>~~MDUC and MEBCO~~</span>, all
> other exposures across studies were measured in urine."
>
> **CLAIM (Methods, para 7).** "For the <span style='color:#999'>~~MDUC and
> VIVA~~</span> cohorts, trace element concentrations were measured from blood
> samples."

Those two sentences name different cohorts, so at most one can be right. Both
are now checkable against the `Matrix_Class` field added on 2026-08-10.

```{r M1}
mx <- EXP[!is.na(Matrix_Class), .(Std, Matrix_Class)] |> unique()
by_std <- mx[, .(matrices = paste(sort(unique(Matrix_Class)), collapse = "+")), by = Std]
blood_studies <- sort(by_std[matrices %like% "Blood|Serum|Plasma", Std])
urine_only    <- sort(by_std[matrices == "Urine", Std])
list(n_blood_any = length(blood_studies), blood = blood_studies,
     n_urine_only = length(urine_only))
```

```{r M1-record}
hero("M1", "Methods", "Cohorts measuring any exposure in blood/serum/plasma",
     "2 (MDUC, MEBCO)", sprintf("%d cohorts", length(blood_studies)),
     paste("Both Methods sentences are wrong, and they contradict each other. Blood-matrix cohorts are:",
           paste(blood_studies, collapse = ", ")))
hero("M1b", "Methods", "Cohorts measuring exposures only in urine",
     "all others", sprintf("%d cohorts", length(urine_only)),
     "The urine/blood split is not a two-cohort exception; see also A9 in the main ledger.")
```

## M2. Analyte panel size in the models

> **CLAIM.** "The maximum numbers of chemical exposures assessed in our models
> were <span style='color:#999'>~~127~~</span> for children and
> <span style='color:#999'>~~143~~</span> for adults."

```{r M2}
panel <- EXP[!is.na(pid), .(n_analytes = uniqueN(Analyte_Code)), by = .(Pop, Std)]
panel_max <- panel[, .(max_analytes = max(n_analytes),
                       at_study = Std[which.max(n_analytes)]), by = Pop]
# Pooled panel = every analyte available to a model of that population.
pooled <- EXP[!is.na(pid), .(pooled_analytes = uniqueN(Analyte_Code)), by = Pop]
merge(panel_max, pooled, by = "Pop")
```

```{r M2-record}
hero("M2", "Methods", "Max chemical exposures in a child model", "127",
     pooled[Pop == "Child", pooled_analytes],
     "Pooled across the child cohorts. The largest single-cohort child panel is smaller; see the table above.")
hero("M2b", "Methods", "Max chemical exposures in an adult model", "143",
     pooled[Pop == "Adult", pooled_analytes], "as M2")
```

## M3. NHANES overlap

> **CLAIM.** "we used NHANES sampling years from 1999-2006 and the
> <span style='color:#999'>~~28~~</span> exposures that overlapped directly with
> HHEAR analytes."

```{r M3}
nh_path <- file.path(ROOT, "Input/NHANES")
nh_file <- list.files(nh_path, pattern = "\\.RData$", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(nh_file)) {
  NH <- tryCatch(as.data.table(load1(nh_file[1])), error = function(e) NULL)
} else NH <- NULL
if (!is.null(NH) && "Analyte_Code" %in% names(NH)) {
  ov <- intersect(unique(NH$Analyte_Code), unique(EXP$Analyte_Code))
  n_overlap <- length(ov)
} else { ov <- NA_character_; n_overlap <- NA_integer_ }
list(nhanes_files = basename(nh_file), n_overlap = n_overlap)
```

```{r M3-record}
hero("M3", "Methods", "NHANES analytes overlapping HHEAR", "28",
     ifelse(is.na(n_overlap), "NOT LOCATED", n_overlap),
     ifelse(is.na(n_overlap),
            "Could not find the NHANES extract in Input/NHANES with an Analyte_Code column. The figure-1B panel uses its own copy; confirm against that.",
            "Counted as codes present in both the NHANES extract and the harmonized targeted data."))
```

# Part 2 — S1, the combined cohort

## A. Demographic composition

> **CLAIM.** "Adult cohorts range from homogeneous populations, such as ZIP
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~82%~~</span> Hispanic) or CEHC
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~79%~~</span> White), to more diverse cohorts, such
> as CCREOH (<span style='color:#999'>~~23%~~</span> Javanese,
> <span style='color:#999'>~~21%~~</span> Creole). Child cohorts … with NFGS
> comprising <span style='color:#999'>~~31%~~</span> Black participants and
> GOALS being <span style='color:#999'>~~100%~~</span> Hispanic. Educational
> attainment differed … from TEDDY, where <span style='color:#999'>~~55%~~</span>
> of participants had a college degree, to DCHS, where
> <span style='color:#999'>~~80%~~</span> had their highest education as a high
> school degree. … higher-income representation in VIVA
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~83%~~</span> earning >$49,000 annually) and lower
> income distributions in SLC (<span style='color:#999'>~~24%~~</span> earning
> <$25,000 annually)."

```{r A-demo}
demo <- data.frame(
  id     = c("A1","A2","A3","A3b","A4","A5","A6","A7","A8","A9"),
  what   = c("ZIP Hispanic","CEHC White","CCREOH Javanese","CCREOH Creole",
             "NFGS Black","GOALS Hispanic","TEDDY college degree",
             "DCHS high school","VIVA income >$49k","SLC income <$25k"),
  now    = c(topcat("Mat_Race","ZIP"), topcat("Mat_Race","CEHC"),
             topcat("Mat_Race","CCREOH",1), topcat("Mat_Race","CCREOH",2),
             topcat("Child_Race","NFGS"), topcat("Child_Race","GOALS"),
             topcat("Mat_Edu","TEDDY"), topcat("Mat_Edu","DCHS"),
             topcat("Mat_Income","VIVA"), topcat("Mat_Income","SLC")),
  published = c("82%","79%","23%","21%","31%","100%","55%","80%","83%","24%"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
demo
```

The SLC income figure deserves a second look:

```{r A9-slc}
slc <- S[Std == "SLC" & !is.na(Mat_Income) & Mat_Income != "", .N, by = Mat_Income]
slc[, share := pct(100 * N / sum(N), 0)][order(-N)]
```

```{r A-record}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(demo)))
  hero(demo$id[i], "S1", demo$what[i], demo$published[i], demo$now[i], "")
hero("A9note", "S1", "SLC lowest income band — is 24% the right number?", "24%",
     slc[Mat_Income %like% "0_25", share],
     "The published 24% is exactly the share of the MIDDLE band (25-49k), not the lowest. Reads like the wrong row was quoted; the lowest band is much larger.")
```

## B. Arsenic contrast

> **CLAIM.** "average arsenic concentrations in CHARGE were
> <span style='color:#999'>~~76-fold~~</span> higher than in GOC."

```{r B-arsenic}
ars <- EXP[Analyte_Code == "As" & Std %in% c("CHARGE","GOC"),
           .(mean = mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE), n = .N,
             units = paste(unique(Units), collapse = "/")), by = Std]
fold <- ars[Std == "CHARGE", mean] / ars[Std == "GOC", mean]
list(ars = ars, fold = round(fold, 1))
```

```{r B-record}
hero("B1", "S1", "CHARGE vs GOC mean arsenic", "76-fold",
     sprintf("%.1f-fold", fold),
     "NB the two studies record units with different capitalisation (ng/mL vs ng/ml). Harmless here, but it defeats a naive unit check.")
```

# Part 3 — S2, limit of detection

> **CLAIM.** "We found the median percent of results below the LOD was
> <span style='color:#999'>~~8%~~</span>. … with the cohorts NHBCS having the
> highest number of samples below LOD (<span style='color:#999'>~~98%~~</span>),
> specifically for the PFAS panel. This left the cohort with two analytes for
> analysis, <span style='color:#999'>~~cotinene and PFOA~~</span>."

```{r C-lod}
# One value per study x analyte, then the median over those -- this is the unit
# the sentence uses ("percent of results below the LOD" for an analyte).
lod <- EXP[!is.na(Detected), .(pct_below = 100 * mean(!Detected)), by = .(Std, Analyte_Code)]
med_lod <- median(lod$pct_below, na.rm = TRUE)
by_study <- lod[, .(median_pct = round(median(pct_below), 1), n_analytes = .N), by = Std][order(-median_pct)]
list(median_across_all = round(med_lod, 1), worst_studies = head(by_study, 4))
```

```{r C-nhbcs}
# Which NHBCS analytes actually survive? "Not censored in every sample" is too
# weak -- it admits analytes censored in 98% of samples. RULE: usable means
# fewer than half the samples are below the LOD, which is what leaves an analyte
# with a estimable median.
nhbcs <- lod[Std %like% "NHBCS"][order(pct_below)]
usable <- nhbcs[pct_below < 50]
list(all = nhbcs, usable = usable,
     by_arm = usable[, .(analytes = paste(Analyte_Code, collapse = ", ")), by = Std])
```

```{r C-record}
hero("C1", "S2", "Median percent of results below LOD", "8%", pct(med_lod),
     "Per study-analyte. Dropped because the added cohorts detect well and because ATLAA/SWSD LODs were recovered from imputed floors this cycle.")
hero("C2", "S2", "Highest median percent below LOD (NHBCS)", "98%",
     pct(by_study[Std == "NHBCS", median_pct]), "")
hero("C3", "S2", "NHBCS analytes left for analysis (<50% censored)", "2 (cotinine, PFOA)",
     sprintf("%d (%s)", nrow(usable), paste(usable$Analyte_Code, collapse = ", ")),
     "PFOS now clears the threshold as well, and cotinine/NNAL sit in the separate NHBCS_Cot arm rather than in NHBCS itself. The sentence has to say which arm it means: NHBCS proper keeps PFOA and PFOS.")
```

# Part 4 — S3, location

> **CLAIM.** "Location accounted for the greatest distributional contribution in
> comparisons between two international cities
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~25%~~</span>), followed by comparisons between a
> U.S. and an international city (<span style='color:#999'>~~19%~~</span>), and
> was lowest for comparisons between two U.S. cities
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~8%~~</span>)."

Read from the S3D panel's own object. **This panel had a bug**: the US location
whitelist in `Age_Sex_Match_Compare.Rmd` never contained `Atlanta` (ATLAA, new
this cycle) or `Southern_California`, so those cities fell through to
"International" and pulled US-only pairs into the international bucket. Fixed
2026-08-10; the values below are post-fix.

```{r D-loc}
loc <- figdata(file.path(OUT, "Plots/r2_barplot_loc.RData"))
d3 <- loc[, .(mean_pct = round(100 * mean(mean_r2, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
              n_categories = .N), by = Country_Location][order(-mean_pct)]
d3
```

```{r D-record}
gv <- function(k) d3[Country_Location == k, mean_pct]
hero("D1", "S3", "Location contribution, two international cities", "25%", pct(gv("International")),
     "Only 4 exposure categories have international-international matched pairs, so this mean rests on a thin base.")
hero("D2", "S3", "Location contribution, US vs international", "19%", pct(gv("United_States:International")), "")
hero("D3", "S3", "Location contribution, two US cities", "8%", pct(gv("United_States")),
     "More than doubled. Partly the Atlanta/Southern_California whitelist fix, partly the added cohorts.")
```

## ZIP country ordering

> **CLAIM.** "In the ZIP cohort, TCP concentrations differed by country, with the
> highest mean levels observed in
> <span style='color:#999'>~~Brazil, followed by Guatemala, Nicaragua, and Puerto Rico~~</span>."

```{r D-zip}
# The pooled SDOH collapses ZIP's Location to "Central/SouthAmerica"; the
# per-country detail (Brazil, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Puerto Rico) survives only in
# ZIP_SDOH_Clean, so read the country from there.
zc <- as.data.table(load1(file.path(HARM, "ZIP_SDOH_Clean.RData")))
zc <- unique(zc[!is.na(Country), .(pid = as.character(Mat_PID), Country = as.character(Country))])
zip <- merge(EXP[Std == "ZIP" & Analyte_Code == "TCP", .(pid, Concentration)], zc, by = "pid")
zsum <- zip[, .(mean = round(mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE), 3), n = .N),
            by = Country][order(-mean)]
zsum
```

```{r D-zip-record}
hero("D4", "S3", "ZIP TCP country ordering (high to low)",
     "Brazil > Guatemala > Nicaragua > Puerto Rico",
     paste(zsum[[1]], collapse = " > "), "")
```

# Part 5 — S4, secular time

> **CLAIM.** "ranging from a single year in ESPINA to
> <span style='color:#999'>~~15 years~~</span> in OBSS. Sample collection spanned
> from 1985 (NYUWHS), through 2021. … the median year of sample collection was
> 2013 (SD = <span style='color:#999'>~~6~~</span> years), and the median study
> duration for sample collection was five years."

```{r E-time}
Y <- EXP[!is.na(Sample_Collection_Year)]
dur <- Y[, .(distinct_years = uniqueN(Sample_Collection_Year),
             lo = min(Sample_Collection_Year), hi = max(Sample_Collection_Year)), by = Std]
list(longest = dur[order(-distinct_years)][1:3],
     shortest = dur[order(distinct_years)][1:3],
     median_duration = median(dur$distinct_years),
     earliest = dur[which.min(lo), .(Std, lo)],
     latest = max(Y$Sample_Collection_Year))
```

```{r E-record}
hero("E1", "S4", "Longest collection window (OBSS)", "15 years",
     sprintf("%d years", dur[Std == "OBSS", distinct_years]),
     "OBSS now reaches 2021. Confirm those 2021 samples are in scope for this paper.")
hero("E2", "S4", "Shortest collection window (ESPINA)", "1 year",
     sprintf("%d year", dur[Std == "ESPINA", distinct_years]), "")
hero("E3", "S4", "Median study duration", "5 years",
     sprintf("%g years", median(dur$distinct_years)), "")
hero("E4", "S4", "Collection span", "1985 (NYUWHS) - 2021",
     sprintf("%g (%s) - %g", dur[which.min(lo), lo], dur[which.min(lo), Std], max(Y$Sample_Collection_Year)), "")
```

## Mother-child contrast

> **CLAIM.** "The largest difference in average concentration occurred in
> cotinine (HCOTT) (<span style='color:#999'>~~32.47~~</span> ng/mL vs
> <span style='color:#999'>~~1.99~~</span> ng/mL in mothers and children). The
> smallest difference … was pentachlorophenol (PCP), with a mean concentration of
> <span style='color:#999'>~~0.018~~</span> ng/mL in the maternal group and
> <span style='color:#999'>~~0.019~~</span> in children."

```{r E-dyad}
dy <- EXP[Std %in% c("DCHS","ELEMENT") & !is.na(Concentration),
          .(mean = mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(Std, Analyte_Code, Pop)]
dw <- dcast(dy, Std + Analyte_Code ~ Pop, value.var = "mean")
dw <- dw[!is.na(Adult) & !is.na(Child)]
dw[, ratio := pmax(Adult, Child) / pmin(Adult, Child)]
list(largest_gap = dw[order(-ratio)][1:3],
     smallest_gap = dw[order(ratio)][1:3],
     hcott = dw[Analyte_Code == "HCOTT"], pcp = dw[Analyte_Code == "PCP"])
```

```{r E-dyad-record}
hc <- dw[Analyte_Code == "HCOTT"]; pc <- dw[Analyte_Code == "PCP"]
hero("E5", "S4", "HCOTT mean, mothers", "32.47 ng/mL", sprintf("%.2f ng/mL", hc$Adult), "")
hero("E6", "S4", "HCOTT mean, children", "1.99 ng/mL", sprintf("%.2f ng/mL", hc$Child), "")
hero("E7", "S4", "PCP mean, mothers", "0.018 ng/mL", sprintf("%.3f ng/mL", pc$Adult), "")
hero("E8", "S4", "PCP mean, children", "0.019 ng/mL", sprintf("%.3f ng/mL", pc$Child), "")
hero("E9", "S4", "Is PCP still the smallest gap?", "yes",
     ifelse(dw[order(ratio)][1, Analyte_Code] == "PCP", "yes",
            sprintf("no - smallest is now %s", dw[order(ratio)][1, Analyte_Code])), "")
```

# Part 6 — S5, demographics

## Within-cohort dispersion

> **CLAIM.** "The largest spread of concentrations within studies are in the
> cohorts MDUC (<span style='color:#999'>~~3.7~~</span>) and DAPS
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~3.7~~</span>), with the lowest being in MEBCO
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~1.2~~</span>) and TSIC
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~1.4~~</span>)."

The Methods define this as the square root of the summed variance of the top 10
PCs. **The code does something different**: it takes each individual's Euclidean
distance in the top-10 PC space and averages within a study. The published
numbers match the code, not the Methods.

```{r F-spread}
sp <- figdata(file.path(OUT, "summ_socio_ridge.RData"))
spread <- sp[, .(mean_dist = round(mean(PCA_Dist, na.rm = TRUE), 1), n = .N), by = Study][order(-mean_dist)]
list(top = head(spread, 4), bottom = tail(spread, 4), n_studies = nrow(spread))
```

```{r F-spread-record}
gs <- function(s) spread[Study == s, mean_dist]
hero("F1", "S5", "Largest within-study spread", "MDUC 3.7, DAPS 3.7",
     sprintf("DAPS %.1f, MDUC %.1f", gs("DAPS"), gs("MDUC")),
     "DAPS and MDUC swap places. Still the top two.")
hero("F2", "S5", "Smallest within-study spread", "MEBCO 1.2, TSIC 1.4",
     sprintf("MEBCO %.1f, TSIC %.1f", gs("MEBCO"), gs("TSIC")), "")
hero("F3", "S5", "Cohorts in the dispersion figure", "34", nrow(spread),
     "FIXED 2026-08-10. Sociodemo_PCA ordered the y axis with a hand-written study_order vector and factor(levels=study_order) turned every unlisted cohort into NA, which the next filter deleted. Four cohorts were vanishing: GRAPHS, ATLAA, SWSD and also DISCOVER, which predates this cycle. The list is now extended from the data with a message and a stopifnot, so it cannot happen silently again. The reported extremes are unchanged -- all four land mid-range.")
```

## Sociodemographic model contributions

> **CLAIM.** "Sampling year alone accounted for an average of
> <span style='color:#999'>~~24.7%~~</span> of the total distributional
> variability measured across studies. However, this quantity ranged from
> <span style='color:#999'>~~83% in NASH~~</span> … to
> <span style='color:#999'>~~2.5% in NFGS~~</span> … The maximum distributional
> contribution attributable to comprehensive demographic models was observed in
> OBSS (<span style='color:#999'>~~18%~~</span>), while VAPS showed minimal
> contribution (<span style='color:#999'>~~0.2%~~</span>)."

```{r F-models}
byst <- figdata(file.path(OUT, "Plots/R2_Barplot_ByStudy.RData"))
# "share of the total distributional variability" = the sampling-year slice as a
# fraction of that study's total, which is the frac column, not the raw pseudo-R2.
# A study whose ONLY fitted component is sampling year trivially reads 100%.
# Those are uninformative, so the range is taken over studies that actually have
# a demographic model to compare the year term against.
multi <- byst[, .(n_components = uniqueN(Model_Type[contrib > 0])), by = Study][n_components >= 2, Study]
sy <- byst[Model_Type == "SY" & Study %in% multi,
           .(Study, share_pct = round(100 * frac, 1))][order(-share_pct)]
tot <- byst[, .(total_pct = round(100 * max(total_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 1)), by = Study][order(-total_pct)]
list(mean_sy_share = round(mean(sy$share_pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
     sy_top = head(sy, 4), sy_bottom = tail(sy, 3),
     total_top = head(tot, 3), total_bottom = tail(tot, 3))
```

```{r F-models-record}
hero("F4", "S5", "Mean sampling-year share of total", "24.7%",
     pct(mean(sy$share_pct, na.rm = TRUE)), "")
```

# Part 7 — S5(bis), power

The within-study and between-study power arrays in `Power_Output/` were last run
on the cluster on 11-12 May 2026, which is **before** GRAPHS, ATLAA and SWSD were
added. They were the last figures still rendering from pre-addition data. Re-run
locally on 2026-08-10 into `Power_Output_2026-08/`; the May results are left
untouched.

```{r G-setup}
newdir <- file.path(OUT, "Power_Output_2026-08")
w_new  <- file.path(newdir, "targeted_quantile_power_results.csv")
b_new  <- file.path(newdir, "Between_Study/between_study_quantile_power_results.csv")

# Range across quantiles, reported the way the sentences do: median power at the
# weakest and strongest tau, each with its IQR.
rng <- function(D) {
  s <- D[, .(med = 100 * median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
             iqr = IQR(power, na.rm = TRUE)), by = tau][order(med)]
  sprintf("%.0f%% (IQR %.2f) at tau %.2f - %.0f%% (IQR %.2f) at tau %.2f",
          s[1, med], s[1, iqr], s[1, tau], s[.N, med], s[.N, iqr], s[.N, tau])
}
```

## Within-study power (fig. S14)

> **CLAIM.** "In the child panel, median power ranged from
> <span style='color:#999'>~~84% (IQR = 0.40)~~</span> at the 0.95 quantile to
> <span style='color:#999'>~~96% (IQR = 0.27)~~</span>. In the adult panel …
> ranging from <span style='color:#999'>~~98% (IQR = 0.13)~~</span> to
> <span style='color:#999'>~~100% (IQR = 0.10)~~</span>. Across individual
> cohorts, <span style='color:#999'>~~65%~~</span> of cohort-quantile
> combinations achieved greater than 90% power. The lowest median power … was
> observed in ELEMENT (<span style='color:#999'>~~9%, IQR = 0.14~~</span>) and
> VAPS (<span style='color:#999'>~~17%, IQR = 0.32~~</span>)."

```{r G-within}
W <- fread(w_new)[analysis == "within_study_demographics" & !is.na(power)]
by_tau <- W[, .(median_power = round(100 * median(power), 0),
                IQR = round(IQR(power), 2)), by = .(panel, tau)][order(panel, tau)]
combos <- W[, .(med = median(power)), by = .(study, tau, panel)]
by_study <- W[, .(median_power = round(100 * median(power), 0),
                  IQR = round(IQR(power), 2)), by = study][order(median_power)]
list(n_studies = uniqueN(W$study), by_tau = by_tau,
     pct_combos_over_90 = round(100 * mean(combos$med > 0.90), 1),
     weakest_cohorts = head(by_study, 4))
```

**Read the next number before you use any of the power values.** Nine
study-panel combinations returned `successful_sims = 0` — every one of their 200
simulation replicates failed, so they carry no power estimate at all. The May
run had none. All nine are *existing* cohorts, not the three added ones, so this
is a regression in the current data or model setup rather than a consequence of
the additions. Every power number below is computed over the surviving
study-panels, and the cohorts listed are simply absent from figure S14B.

```{r G-dropouts}
# Count dropouts on the RAW file. W has already had !is.na(power) applied, so
# counting on W would always report zero -- the rows we are looking for are
# exactly the ones that filter removed.
W_raw <- fread(w_new)[analysis == "within_study_demographics"]
sp <- W_raw[, .(median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
                successful = sum(successful_sims, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(panel, study)]
dropped <- sp[is.na(median_power)]
old_w <- file.path(OUT, "Power_Output/targeted_quantile_power_results.csv")
old_dropped <- if (file.exists(old_w)) {
  O <- fread(old_w)[analysis == "within_study_demographics"]
  O[, .(m = median(power, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(panel, study)][is.na(m), .N]
} else NA_integer_
list(dropped_now = dropped, n_dropped_now = nrow(dropped),
     n_dropped_in_may_run = old_dropped)
```

```{r G-within-record}

     "local re-run 2026-08-10",
     "The May cluster run predated GRAPHS, ATLAA and SWSD; S8/S9 were the last figures still drawing on pre-addition data. Re-run into Power_Output_2026-08/, leaving the May output intact.")
hero("G7", "S5-power", "Study-panels with zero successful simulations", "0 (May run)",
     sprintf("%d (%s)", nrow(dropped), paste(sort(unique(dropped$study)), collapse = ", ")),
     "REGRESSION, and it is not the new cohorts -- all nine are pre-existing. No single covariate or sample-year pattern explains it (DAPS fits on 4 distinct years, CCREOH fails on 4). Until this is diagnosed, treat every S5-power number as provisional: they are computed on the survivors, and G5 in particular is sensitive to which cohorts are in the denominator.")
hero("G3", "S5-power", "Child within-study power range", "84% (IQR 0.40) - 96% (IQR 0.27)",
     rng(W[panel == "child"]),

     rng(W[panel == "maternal"]), "as G3")
```

## Between-study power (fig. S13)

> **CLAIM.** "In the adult panel, the median power … ranging from
> <span style='color:#999'>~~89% (IQR = 0)~~</span> at the 0.05 quantile to
> <span style='color:#999'>~~97% (IQR = 0)~~</span> at the 0.75 quantile …
> where median power ranged from <span style='color:#999'>~~91%~~</span> at the
> 0.05 quantile to <span style='color:#999'>~~97%~~</span> at the 0.95 quantile."

**This one has to go back to the cluster.** The within-study array re-ran
locally in an hour, but the between-study array fits *pooled* cross-cohort
models — median n = 1,491 against a few hundred within-study — and 200 censored
quantile simulations of that size take roughly 15 minutes each. At 1,867 tasks
that is about two days with the machine fully committed, so I stopped it. The
SLURM array it was written for is the right way to run it:

```bash
sbatch Coding/Paper1_Submission2/submit_betweenstudy_quantile_power_array.sh
```

One portability fix is already in: `BetweenStudy_Quantile_Power_Array.R` resolved
its own directory from `commandArgs()`, which Rscript hands back with spaces
encoded as `~+~`. The cluster path has no spaces so it never showed there, but
it failed immediately under `My Drive`. That is now decoded before use, so the
script runs from either place.

```{r G-between}
between_ready <- file.exists(b_new)
if (between_ready) {
  B <- fread(b_new)[!is.na(power)]
  B[, .(median_power = round(100 * median(power), 0), IQR = round(IQR(power), 2)),
    by = .(panel, tau)][order(panel, tau)]
} else {
  cat("NOT RE-RUN - figure S13 still renders from the May 2026 cluster output,\n",
      "which predates GRAPHS, ATLAA and SWSD. Do not quote S8 numbers yet.\n")
}
```

```{r G-between-record}
  hero("G2", "S5-power", "Child between-study power range", "91% - 97%",

} else {

  hero("G2", "S5-power", "Child between-study power range", "91% - 97%",
       "NOT RE-RUN", "as G1")
```

## Cumulative exposure score

> **CLAIM.** "Individuals who had all measured exposures in the top quartile …
> had an average score of <span style='color:#999'>~~69~~</span>, those with 50%
> … <span style='color:#999'>~~52~~</span>, and those with none
> <span style='color:#999'>~~34~~</span>. … an individual with only 10% … had an
> overall score of <span style='color:#999'>~~60~~</span>. … the amount of
> variation in the cumulative score contributed by demographic models ranges from
> <span style='color:#999'>~~0.02 (ELEMENT)~~</span> to
> <span style='color:#999'>~~0.23 (SICAS)~~</span>. Age provided a baseline of on
> average <span style='color:#999'>~~29%~~</span> … sex
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~14%~~</span>), education
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~53%~~</span>) or race
> (<span style='color:#999'>~~19.8~~</span>) … an additional
> <span style='color:#999'>~~20%~~</span>."

Regenerated 2026-08-11. The burden pipeline and its by-cohort ExWAS are now
ported to Submission 2 (`Exposure_Burden_Creation_Perc_S2.Rmd`,
`ByCohort_BurdenExWAS_S2.Rmd`, `BurdenByStudy_CompareR2_S2.Rmd`), so these are
computed from current data rather than the April-2025 outputs.

**The published paragraph says "quartile" four times.** The Methods, the figure
caption and the code all use **tertiles**, cut at 33.33 and 66.66. The word is
wrong, not the analysis.

```{r H-burden}
# Each measured exposure is Low/Medium/High by its percentile in the pooled
# cohort; prop_high is the share of a person's exposures in the top tertile.
bl <- function(f, idcol) {
  D  <- as.data.table(load1(file.path(OUT, f)))
  pc <- grep("_Percentile$", names(D), value = TRUE)
  m  <- as.matrix(D[, ..pc])
  data.table(prop_high = rowSums(m > 66.66, na.rm = TRUE) / rowSums(!is.na(m)),
             score = D$Burden_Adj)
}
P <- rbind(bl("Burden_Child.RData", "Child_PID"), bl("Burden_Mat.RData", "Mat_PID"))
P <- P[is.finite(prop_high) & !is.na(score)]
score_at <- function(lo, hi) mean(P[prop_high >= lo & prop_high <= hi, score])
list(n = nrow(P),
     all_high = round(score_at(0.999, 1)), half = round(score_at(0.45, 0.55)),
     none = round(score_at(0, 0.001)), ten_pct_mean = round(score_at(0.05, 0.15)),
     ten_pct_max = round(max(P[prop_high >= 0.05 & prop_high <= 0.15, score])),
     correlation = round(cor(P$prop_high, P$score), 3))
```

```{r H-burden-demo}
BR <- figdata(file.path(OUT, "R2_Barplot_Burden.RData"))
BR[, Study := as.character(Study)]
BR[, frac := contrib / sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE), by = Study]
tot <- BR[, .(total = round(max(total_R2, na.rm = TRUE), 3)), by = Study][order(total)]
shr <- function(m) round(100 * mean(BR[Model_Type == m, frac], na.rm = TRUE), 1)
list(range = tot[c(1, .N)],
     age = shr("Age"), age_sex = shr("Age_Sex"), age_edu = shr("Age_Edu"),
     age_race = shr("Age_Race"), additional = shr("Additional_Socio_Values"))
```

```{r H-burden-record}

     round(score_at(0.999, 1)), "Only 101 individuals have every measured exposure in the top tertile.")
hero("H7", "S7", "Score, 50% in top tertile", "52", round(score_at(0.45, 0.55)), "")
hero("H8", "S7", "Score, no exposures in top tertile", "34", round(score_at(0, 0.001)), "")
hero("H9", "S7", "Score for an individual at 10% top-tertile", "60",
     sprintf("mean %d, up to %d", round(score_at(0.05, 0.15)),
             round(max(P[prop_high >= 0.05 & prop_high <= 0.15, score]))),
     "The published 60 reads as a single illustrative individual, not an average. The mean at 10% is much lower; the paragraph's actual point -- wide spread in score at low top-tertile share -- still holds, since scores in that band run from single digits to the low 60s.")

     "0.02 (ELEMENT) - 0.23 (SICAS)",
     sprintf("%.3f (%s) - %.3f (%s)", tot[1, total], tot[1, Study], tot[.N, total], tot[.N, Study]),
     sprintf("SICAS remains the maximum. ELEMENT is now %.3f and is no longer the minimum. NB the published 0.02 for ELEMENT matches neither this run nor the 2025 one (0.002), so check that value's provenance.", tot[Study == "ELEMENT", total]))
hero("H11", "S7", "Age baseline share", "29%", pct(shr("Age")), "")
hero("H12", "S7", "Single-feature shares (sex / education / race)", "14% / 53% / 19.8%",

Read instead as a percent CHANGE from the age-only model it gives values in the thousands, because Age alone explains almost nothing in several cohorts. Confirm which was meant.")
hero("H13", "S7", "All features additional", "20%", pct(shr("Additional_Socio_Values")), "")
```

# Part 9 — Supplementary tables

The Doc carries Tables 1 and 2 inline; the front matter promises S1 to S8 and
the Methods cite a Table S9, so the rest live elsewhere. Only the two inline
tables are regenerated here.

## Supplementary Table 1 — cohort demographics

**Rule used.** A participant counts if they have at least one targeted exposure
measurement, keyed on `(Study, PID)` with a trailing `.0` stripped. Education is
coalesced across `Max_Edu`, `Mat_Edu`, `Edu_Max`, `Edu` because no single column
covers every cohort. "College" includes some college and above.

```{r T1}
norm <- function(p) sub("\\.0+$", "", trimws(as.character(p)))
haveC <- unique(paste(EXP$Std, norm(EXP$Child_PID)))
haveM <- unique(paste(EXP$Std, norm(EXP$Mat_PID)))
Sc <- S[!is.na(Child_PID)][paste(Std, norm(Child_PID)) %in% haveC]
Sm <- S[!is.na(Mat_PID)][paste(Std, norm(Mat_PID)) %in% haveM]

COLLEGE <- c("Four_Year_College_Degree","Some_Grad_School","Graduate_School",
             "Some_Graduate_School","Some_College")
HIGHSCH <- c("High_School","Secondary_Education")
LESSHS  <- c("Primary_Education","No_Education","Primary_School")
DROP    <- c("", "NA", "Unknown", "Other / Unknown")

edu_of <- function(D) {
  v <- fcoalesce(as.character(D$Max_Edu), as.character(D$Mat_Edu),
                 as.character(D$Edu_Max), as.character(D$Edu))
  v[!is.na(v) & !v %in% DROP]
}
# Percent is out of NON-MISSING responses, which is what makes the published
# Male/Female pair sum to 100. Passing the raw column would divide by N and the
# two sexes would come to 94%.
cnt <- function(v, lev) {
  v <- v[!is.na(v) & !v %in% DROP]
  n <- length(v); s <- sum(v %in% lev)
  sprintf("%s (%.2f%%)", format(s, big.mark = ","), 100 * s / n) }

# Income: bracket labels only. CCREOH still carries raw numeric codes 1-9, which
# belong to no bracket and are excluded rather than silently binned.
UNDER50 <- c("0_25k","25_49k")
OVER50  <- c("Over_49k","50_74k","75_99k","Over_100k","100_124k","Over_125k")
inc_of <- function(D) { v <- as.character(D$Mat_Income); v[v %in% c(UNDER50, OVER50)] }

T1 <- function(D, pop) {
  e <- edu_of(D); i <- inc_of(D)
  ea <- e[e %in% c(COLLEGE, HIGHSCH, LESSHS)]
  age <- if (pop == "Child") D$Child_Age else D$Mat_Age
  data.frame(
    Variable = c("N", "Male", "Female", "Age: Mean (SD)",
                 "Income under 50k", "Income over 50k",
                 "College education", "High school education", "Less than high school"),
    Value = c(format(nrow(D), big.mark = ","),
              if (pop == "Child") cnt(as.character(D$Child_Sex), "M") else "N/A",
              if (pop == "Child") cnt(as.character(D$Child_Sex), "F") else "N/A",
              sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), sd(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
              cnt(i, UNDER50), cnt(i, OVER50),
              cnt(ea, COLLEGE), cnt(ea, HIGHSCH), cnt(ea, LESSHS)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
tab1 <- merge(T1(Sc, "Child"), T1(Sm, "Adult"), by = "Variable",
              suffixes = c("_Child", "_Maternal"), sort = FALSE)
names(tab1) <- c("Demographic Variable", "Child-based Cohorts", "Maternal Cohorts")
tab1$`Published (Child)` <- c("9,664","4,736 (52.3%)","4,325 (47.7%)","6.5 (4.9)",
  "1327 (71.65%)","525 (28.35%)","2005 (42.06%)","1800 (37.76%)","962 (20.18%)")
tab1$`Published (Maternal)` <- c("11,764","N/A","N/A","31.34 (14.03)",
  "1818 (53.96%)","1551 (46.04%)","3664 (59.4%)","2066 (33.5%)","438 (7.1%)")
knitr::kable(tab1)
```

```{r T1-race}
race_tab <- function(D, col) {
  v <- as.character(D[[col]]); v <- v[!is.na(v) & !v %in% DROP]
  t <- sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE)
  data.frame(Group = names(t), N = as.integer(t),
             Pct = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * as.numeric(t) / length(v)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
list(child = race_tab(Sc, "Child_Race"), maternal = race_tab(Sm, "Mat_Race"))
```

```{r T1-write}
write.csv(race_tab(Sc, "Child_Race"), file.path(HN, "SuppTable1_race_child.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(race_tab(Sm, "Mat_Race"), file.path(HN, "SuppTable1_race_maternal.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("written to", HN, "\n")
```

```{r T1-record}
hero("T1b", "Table S1", "Maternal cohort N", "11,764", format(nrow(Sm), big.mark = ","), "")
hero("T1c", "Table S1", "Education denominators reproduce?", "n=4,767 (child)",
     sprintf("n=%s", format(length(edu_of(Sc)[edu_of(Sc) %in% c(COLLEGE, HIGHSCH, LESSHS)]), big.mark = ",")),
     "NOT RECONCILED. No combination of education columns I tried reproduces the published denominator, so the published table used a rule I could not recover. The proportions are in the same region; the counts are not. Confirm which column the original table read before using these rows.")
hero("T1d", "Table S1", "CCREOH income coding", "-",
     sprintf("%d rows with raw numeric codes", S[Std == "CCREOH" & grepl("^[0-9]+$", as.character(Mat_Income)), .N]),
     "CCREOH income is still raw ordinal codes 1-9 while every other cohort uses bracket labels. They belong to no bracket and are dropped from the income rows, so CCREOH is silently absent from that part of the table.")
```

## Supplementary Table 2 — chemical crosswalk

```{r T2}
CW <- fread(file.path(HARM, "Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv"))
measured <- unique(EXP$Analyte_Code)

# The _BR (breast milk) and _DBS (dried blood spot) codes are matrix variants of
# a parent analyte, not separate chemicals, and the crosswalk has no row for
# them -- they came out of this table with a blank name, CAS and category.
# Resolve each to its parent and carry the matrix in its own column.
t2 <- data.table(Code = measured[!is.na(measured)])
t2[, Matrix_Variant := fcase(Code %like% "_BR$",  "Breast milk",
                             Code %like% "_DBS$", "Dried blood spot",
                             default = "")]
t2[, Parent := sub("_(BR|DBS)$", "", Code)]
t2 <- merge(t2, CW[, .(Parent = Code, Full_Name, CAS, Category)], by = "Parent", all.x = TRUE)
t2 <- t2[, .(Code, Full_Name, CAS, Category, Matrix_Variant)][order(Category, Code)]
write.csv(t2, file.path(HN, "SuppTable2_regenerated.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

unresolved <- t2[is.na(Category) | Category == "", Code]
list(n_rows = nrow(t2),
     n_matrix_variants = t2[Matrix_Variant != "", .N],
     still_unresolved = unresolved,
     no_cas = t2[is.na(CAS) | CAS == "NA" | CAS == "", .N],
     by_category = t2[, .N, by = Category][order(-N)])
```

```{r T2-record}
hero("T2b", "Table S2", "PFHP_BR vs PFHp_BR in NHBCS", "-",
     "two distinct analytes, not a duplicate",
     "They differ only by the case of one letter, which is fragile: any toupper() or case-insensitive join anywhere in the pipeline would silently merge them. They are genuinely different (LOD 0.025 vs 0.01) but both are 100% censored, so neither reaches analysis and no result depends on telling them apart today. PFHp has no crosswalk row, so it stays uncategorised here rather than being force-matched to PFHP's metadata.")
hero("T2", "Table S2", "Rows in the chemical crosswalk", "-", nrow(t2),
     sprintf("%d rows are matrix variants (_BR breast milk, _DBS dried blood spot) that the crosswalk has no entry for; they are now resolved to their parent analyte and flagged in a Matrix_Variant column. %d rows still have no CAS and %d no category at all.",
             t2[Matrix_Variant != "", .N],
             t2[is.na(CAS) | CAS == "NA" | CAS == "", .N], length(unresolved)))
```

# Part 10 — Figure S20, sample matrix and the location signal

New supplementary figure, added to the set 2026-08-11. It was produced earlier
in this cycle (`Coding/Matrix_Stratified/`) but had no S-number and no entry
here, so its numbers were untracked. Numbered **S15** rather than inserted next
to S3 so nothing downstream renumbers — the existing S-numbering already needs
seven corrections (Part 0) and adding an eighth helps nobody.

- Figure: `Output/Matrix_Stratified/SuppFig_Matrix_Confound.pdf`
- Caption and paragraph: `Coding/Matrix_Stratified/SUPPLEMENTARY_TEXT.md`
- Regenerate with `Coding/Matrix_Stratified/03_compare_location_contribution.R`

**Unaffected by the 2026-08-10 SDOH change.** The pipeline reads
`Harmonized_SDOH` only for location structure and never touches `Mat_Income`,
which was the sole column the CCREOH fix altered, so the 11:08 build is current.

```{r S15}
mx <- fread(file.path(ROOT, "Output/Matrix_Stratified/location_contribution_by_matrix.csv"))
mx
```

```{r S15-record}
te <- mx[Category == "TraceElements"]
fr <- mx[Category == "FlameRetardants"]
# Classes assayed in a single matrix must land exactly on the pooled value --
# this is the internal control that stratification only moved what it should.
single <- mx[!is.na(published) & abs(urine_minus_published) < 0.05, Category]

hero("S15a", "Fig S20", "Trace elements, location contribution pooled", "-",
     sprintf("%.1f%%", te$published),
     "The published figure, blood and urine cohorts pooled.")
hero("S15b", "Fig S20", "Trace elements, location contribution within urine", "-",
     sprintf("%.1f%% (blood %.1f%%)", te$Urine, te$Blood),
     sprintf("Falls %.1f points once locations are compared within one medium -- roughly a quarter of the pooled estimate is sampling medium, not geography.", -te$urine_minus_published))
hero("S15c", "Fig S20", "Flame retardants, pooled to within-urine", "-",
     sprintf("%.1f%% to %.1f%%", fr$published, fr$Urine),
     "The confound is not unidirectional: pooling with a weaker blood signal had SUPPRESSED this class, so stratifying raises it.")
hero("S15d", "Fig S20", "Single-matrix classes unchanged (internal control)", "-",
     sprintf("%d classes", length(single)),
     paste("Unchanged to the first decimal, as they must be:", paste(single, collapse = ", ")))
hero("S15e", "Fig S20", "Locations contributing more than one matrix", "-", "0",
     "Matrix is perfectly confounded with location, which is why the pooled location estimate is an upper bound.")
```

```{r ledger-table, echo=FALSE}
show_tab <- function(d) {
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    id = d$id, quantity = d$claim,
    `WRITE THIS` = paste0("**", d$now, "**"),
    was = ifelse(d$published %in% c("-", "", NA), "",
                 paste0("<span style='color:#999'><s>", d$published, "</s></span>")),
    why = d$note, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
}
```

### Safe to write with

```{r t-safe, echo=FALSE}
show_tab(tab[tab$status == "SAFE", ])
```

### Value changed materially

```{r t-changed, echo=FALSE}
show_tab(tab[tab$status == "CHANGED", ])
```

### The sentence needs rewriting, not just renumbering

```{r t-rewrite, echo=FALSE}
show_tab(tab[tab$status == "REWRITE", ])
```

### Needs your decision

```{r t-check, echo=FALSE}
show_tab(tab[tab$status %in% c("CHECK","FLAG"), ])
```

### Do not quote yet

```{r t-blocked, echo=FALSE}
show_tab(tab[tab$status == "BLOCKED", ])
```

```{r corrected, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
g <- function(id) if (is.na(V[id])) paste0("<<", id, " missing>>") else V[id]
gn <- function(id, k = 1) {
  n <- regmatches(g(id), gregexpr("[0-9]+\\.?[0-9]*", g(id)))[[1]]
  if (length(n) < k) paste0("<<", id, " no number ", k, ">>") else n[k]
}
```
